text:
MPC gained about 0.3% today, extending a strong two-week rally of 7.8%. The stock has risen steadily as diesel prices hit record highs due to refinery disruptions from the Ukraine and Iran conflicts, while U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity—near maximum utilization. For a refiner like MPC, higher diesel prices and tight supply mean wider profit margins on fuel production, which directly boosts earnings.

The broader backdrop strengthens this tailwind: geopolitical tensions are knocking refineries offline globally (Ukraine hitting Russian facilities, Iran sanctions limiting output), and the U.S. has just secured a Venezuela oil deal that could reshape hemispheric energy flows. These supply constraints keep refineries profitable even as crude oil sits around $91–96 per barrel, because the gap between crude costs and finished fuel prices—the margin refiners pocket—has widened sharply.
